beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output. You need a check.
beats.got: Output alone doesn't show safety, so a separate check is needed.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** residual risk: what is left, and what future sessions need before touching the system
beats.got: A list of six verbs. The residual-risk one is the only one that sounds useful to me.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I should list my own worries before the agent tells me what they are.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent's text becomes real actions through a harness, so a vague description leads to a bad action. Useful, but I can't tell yet whether it matters for my pricing work.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: The unease about my own agents is the point of this module.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: nothing new. My CFO and I already know this.

beats.trigger: The dangerous move is getting your agent to *decide* to do something harmful with access it has, through well-formed English in a document it reads.
beats.got: A document the agent reads can steer it. That's a risk for the churn article and any other source I feed it.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: Five named mitigations I can put in a risk memo. Gate and scope are the ones I'd use.

beats.trigger: *the residual risk is X; if Y happens, we made it less likely, not prevented it.*
beats.got: A sentence format I can put in front of my CFO. It names what is left and who accepted it.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: Reducing access limits the damage, at the cost of usefulness.

beats.trigger: Every door you don't open is a residual risk you don't have to name, mitigate or re-test.
beats.got: Don't connect what you don't need. Sensible, but I'd say it in one sentence, not four.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff. It will still be complex when the next agent gets built.
beats.got: nothing new. It repeats the loop for the third time, and the line about complexity is filler.

beats.trigger: a skill is a reusable check you run again instead of re-prompting from memory.
beats.got: A skill is a saved method the agent loads, so it isn't another prompt. I could hand that to my team.

beats.trigger: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: Some policy rules the agent can check from files, and others it can't.

beats.trigger: Push back on anything that sounds like a generic GDPR brochure.
beats.got: I tell it what matters at Nordveil (dispatch customer data, pricing pilot numbers) and it shapes the check around that.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: A long Q&A. I'd rather give it three bullets and let it draft.

beats.trigger: *"You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."*
beats.got: I can hand back decisions I can't judge, and I can say so without losing control.

beats.trigger: Run `ls .claude/skills/agent-audit/` to confirm.
beats.got: Install steps differ by runtime. Mechanical.

beats.trigger: Agent mitigations sit on top of normal company controls, not in place of them.
beats.got: The skill carries the judgment, and it doesn't replace the controls IT already has.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: I'm not expected to pass. I'm expected to run the loop on my own system.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: Checking that the skill loads. Setup.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The audit flags rows I thought were fine and marks some I thought were settled as undecidable. That's the contradiction-finding I like.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: A ranked list of how my own system could be misled. I'd show it to my security lead.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: I fix one risk, write down what remains, and sign it. That's decision hygiene I'd actually do.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report. Walk in with that.
beats.got: Take the specific open question to legal or security with the evidence, not a vague worry.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent. You must do the work.
beats.got: I only did one risk. Production needs all of them. It's honest, but it's also a lot of work.

beats.trigger: Certainty is not on offer. The discipline is the loop: assess, mitigate, reassess the residual, decide.
beats.got: nothing new. Fourth time I've read the loop.

beats.trigger: Two things travel: the reusable check, and the root instructions file's rules for the risk you found.
beats.got: The agent adds rules to my instructions file from what we found. The next session starts with them.

beats.trigger: Their agent loads the same method by name without your prompt history.
beats.got: I could give my fourteen people the same pricing-brief method as a skill. It's close to what I came for, but sharing it is left to Module 7.

beats.trigger: Mitigations add to security controls, never replace them.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a summary of what I just did.

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors. Your call.
beats.got: Homework: one sentence per case on the missing organisational check.

beats.trigger: What check was missing around the agent's output?
beats.got: Two cases to read, with the question I need to answer.

take_homes: Run the audit as a loop: assess, mitigate one risk, write down what remains and who accepted it. The residual-risk sentence is what I can show my CFO.
Text the agent reads can steer it, so the sources I feed my pricing agent (like the churn article) are an attack surface. Giving it less access is the cheapest fix.
A skill is a saved method I can hand to my team. The audit skill carries our rules, and the next agent gets checked the same way.

monday.move: Run the agent-audit skill on the pilot-cohort brief agent, pick the top risk, apply a gate or scope cut, and write the residual sentence.
monday.who: Me, then send the report to our security lead and the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: One mitigation applied and one residual risk written and accepted on record. I don't try to fix everything.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the skill and context files, so it would live on my machine only.

misconception.why: The audit found rows I'd called settled and flagged real risks that no prompt wording could have fixed. That's about access, sources and checks, not better prompts. I'm not fully convinced, because the module never says that outright.

one_line: Good hour for anyone with an agent near real data. It makes you name the risk you're leaving in, but the loop gets explained four times and I'd cut two.
